task.title: P6-188 review leftovers: teardown from==to guard, delete TOCTOU scope, board-path CI coverage
task.description: Filed from the P6-188 adversarial review (2026-08-09). Items: (1) RESOLVED WON'T-FIX (maintainer ruling, Dylan, 2026-08-10): teardown's missing to_collection_id != collection_id guard was also queue task P6-112, deleted by ruling — no public API exists or is planned, both clients exclude self-destination, and zero from==to rows have ever existed in the ledger (verified live against dev 2026-08-10; the earlier 'exists in the wild' review claim was wrong). Revisit only if an API is ever exposed or such a row ever appears. (2) delete_collection's FOR UPDATE covers only the subject collection row; a concurrent add_holding into the collection between snapshot and the deleted_at stamp is silently hidden (and a concurrently-hidden child can appear in the receipt's reparented list without having been re-parented) — alpha-tolerable single-user race; consider locking holdings or re-checking counts before commit. (3) the delete planner's apply() model ignores boards, so the destination-side Board::Main collapse in the executor is exercised only by the #[ignore]d delete_live dev test, never in CI — extend the planner model or add a board-aware no-DB test. (4) undo_delete's desire re-insert (DO UPDATE SET quantity = quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity) can overflow int4 on a near-i32::MAX crafted receipt — rolls back, nothing stored, but surfaces as an Upstream 500 instead of a Validation 400; add an upper bound or catch the overflow into a typed error. (5) accepted-widening note: reparent_is_safe admits current-siblings (with reparent_to = None, every top-level non-Inbox collection) — verified acyclic and drag-repairable, deliberately NOT tightened. Also note: the P6-188 wire change (POST body now optional-but-validated) is self-healing for stale APKs. Specs: specs/collection-deletion.md. (6) Appended from the P6-113 review (2026-08-10): the three #[ignore]d delete_live tokio tests share the SCRATCH prefix, dev user, and whole-table counts() baselines, so cargo test -- --ignored delete_live is mutually destructive under the default parallel harness — serialize them (serial_test or a shared mutex) or give each its own prefix and scoped baselines.
